parts:
I am sorry but the current version of rmr is not compatible with windows.

Sent from a phone

On Dec 27, 2012 3:45 PM, "Brian Tieman" <bjti...@gmail.com> wrote:
I've managed to get rmr2 to work on my test linux cluster.  From a unix R instance, I can write/run the mapreduce examples from the wiki.  I'd like to be able to run them from a Windows installation of R. 

When trying to install rmr2 on windows, the compile fails:

> install.packages("C:/Users/BT023373/Documents/Downloads/R/rmr2_2.0.2.tar.gz", repos=NULL, type="source")
* installing *source* package 'rmr2' ...
** libs
g++  -I"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-215~1.2/include" -DNDEBUG       `C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-215~1.2/bin/Rscript -e "Rcpp:::CxxFlags()"`   -O2 -Wall  -mtune=core2 -c dataframe-to-list.cpp -o dataframe-to-list.o
g++: Files/R/R-2.15.2/library/Rcpp/include: No such file or directory
In file included from dataframe-to-list.cpp:15:0:
dataframe-to-list.h:18:18: fatal error: Rcpp.h: No such file or directory
compilation terminated.

It looks like the problem is the include directory for Rcpp is not enclosed in quotes/not space sterilized like the other paths in the build command.  Being new to R, I don't understand where the compile command line is being built.  Is there someplace I can edit (hack if need be) to fix-up the include path?  I was able to get rhbase to build and install ok (though it hangs when running which I've asked about in another thread) so, in general at least, I can compile R packages.  Just looks like there's a path name problem with this one.

Thanks for any assistance in this!

Brian

messages.author: 1149d0e1f0a317c8
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#472] Error compiling rmr2 on windows.
parts:
I'm running CDH4 under Cygwin on Windows just fine.  I've run apache hadoop in the past but needed to fixup the hadoop and hbase scripts for windows paths.  There's code in there for cygwin but since it's not much used, it's sometimes out of date.  I don't generally run hadoop services on Windows because we have several linux clusters but I do develop for Hadoop/HBase almost exclusively from my windows machine by connecting to the cluster services.

Once I hacked hdfs.init() to handle building the classpath correctly for windows, it worked perfectly well. 

I do have a problem with rhbase hanging but it compiles without problem.  It appears the hanging is within boost when it tries to initialize the connection.  I'm guessing it has to do with the firewall on windows but I haven't dug deeper to see for sure.  I am running the thrift server on my Windows box and I can loop back through it from a linux instance of R where rhbase is working properly.

I may be wrong, but I see no fundamental reason why rmr shouldn't work as well.  I did dig deeper and the compilation problems are an issue with Rcpp and not rmr itself.  Moving my R installation to a path without spaces allowed the build to go further but then I ran into another compile time issue that looks to be Rcpp not doing the right thing under windows.

Since I'm still in the evaluation phase, I punted and moved to running under Virtualbox...which is cumbersome but works well enough.  It's possible that if we decide to adopt R I'll be coming back to these issues but for now, I can run well enough to evaluate what we'd like to see.

Thank you for your help in this!

Brian
